questions.q: What is the Az module actually made of?
options: An umbrella over dozens of service-specific sub-modules, such as Az.Compute and Az.Storage
A single, monolithic module with no internal structure
A renamed copy of the retired AzureRM module with no other changes
A set of cmdlets that only work inside the Azure Cloud Shell
questions.explain: Get-AzVM lives in Az.Compute, Get-AzStorageAccount lives in Az.Storage — Install-Module Az pulls in the whole family of service-specific sub-modules.

questions.q: Why doesn't plain Connect-AzAccount work inside an unattended script that runs on a schedule?
options: It opens an interactive browser sign-in, which has nobody present to complete it
It only works on Linux, never on Windows
It requires a paid Azure support plan to use
It is deprecated and no longer functions in any context
questions.explain: Connect-AzAccount's default flow needs a person to click through a browser prompt — a script running unattended has no one there to do that.

questions.q: What does Connect-AzAccount -ServicePrincipal authenticate as, instead of a person?
options: An application identity, using an app ID and a client secret as credentials
A guest user account with no password
The Azure subscription itself, with no identity at all
A temporary anonymous session that expires in 60 seconds
questions.explain: A service principal is an application identity; the app ID acts as the credential's username and a client secret acts as the password.

options: Pulls the newest version of the Az module down from the PowerShell Gallery
Deletes the Az module entirely from the machine
Only updates Az.Accounts and leaves every other sub-module untouched
Reverts Az back to the AzureRM module
questions.explain: Update-Module -Name Az fetches and installs the latest release from the PowerShell Gallery, replacing the older installed version.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does keeping Az updated matter for automation specifically?
options: Azure ships frequent changes, including documented breaking changes, that can affect unattended scripts with nobody watching the output
Updating Az has no real effect on how scripts behave
Only interactive console sessions are ever affected by module version
Az is updated once a year at most, so this is rarely a concern
questions.explain: The Az module's own release notes document breaking changes release by release, which is a real risk for anything running unattended on a fixed schedule.
